narrative:
The model estimated a 61.9% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt, which is why your law school application was denied. This is a risk estimate, not a certainty: it means the school judged the likelihood of first-try failure to be high enough to outweigh admission.

The strongest factor was your first-year class decile. Being in the second decile—compared with the accepted students’ average of the sixth decile—pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your LSAT score of 35 was the next most influential factor, and it worked in your favor, pushing toward a pass; however, it was not enough to offset the first-year academic signal. Your middle family-income bracket was the third most important factor and added a smaller push toward failure; accepted students were more often upper-middle income.

To improve future applications, focus on what the decision highlights. Ask admissions for feedback, consider intensive LSAT preparation and whether retaking the exam could strengthen your profile, and address the first-year academic record directly—for example, by explaining any circumstances and showing stronger later coursework. You may also strengthen your application through relevant work, stronger recommendations, or additional academic study before reapplying.
